newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CCB finalises alliance with French CLF.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CCB finalises alliance with French CLF.

text.p: Belgian publicly-owned bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) on Wednesday finalised its alliance with French Credit Local de France.
CCB said in a statement both groups had signed a shareholder agreement and the terms of their share exchange.
The banks' shareholders, which specialise in financing local public authorities, gave the go-ahead for the alliance earlier this month.
CCB also set up the boards of directors for the two holding companies which will control the bank after under the new alliance.

The Municipalities Holding, itself 100-percent owned by Belgium's local authorities, will hold 70 percent of CCB Holding. CCB Holding will hold a 50 percent stake in Gemeentekrediet Bank and a 50 percent stake in Credit Local de France Bank.
Credit Local de France Holding will also hold 50 percent stakes in the two operational banks, mirroring the Belgian structure.
The chairman of board of the Municipalities Holding will be Gilbert Mottard. Tony Van Parys will be chairman of CCB Holding, while Guy Spitaels will head the board of CCB Bank.
A 30 percent stake in CCB Holding is set to be listed on the Brussels bourse in the first half of November.
